summary: Warm Springs Reservation lookout in Wasco County: a tower begun in 1936 and dated 1938 by the register, now gone; tribal land, so visits need the reservation's permission.

facts.design: 90 ft three-legged treated timber tower with 6x6 ft cab and a cabin
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin are gone per the register and firelookout.com; no source describes what remains on the site

access.note: On Warm Springs Indian Reservation (tribal) land; no public access is described in the sources

events.note: Construction of an 80-foot wooden tower started in spring 1936, per the Annual Forestry and Grazing Report F.Y. 1936 as quoted by Oregon Lookouts
90-foot three-legged treated timber tower with 6x6 ft cab and a cabin (register and firelookout.com)

corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com both give a 90-foot tower (27.4 m). The record's 24.4 m equals the 80-foot tower in the 1936 construction notice, which is a plan rather than the built structure. Needs a human decision.

sources.title: Hehe Butte Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Thin record: three sources, two of them short register-style entries. Staffing, fire history and removal date are not found; a WebSearch and a Wikipedia check turned up nothing more. Height and start year conflict: 90 ft and 1938 (register, firelookout.com) against an 80-foot tower and spring 1936 start (1936 forestry report, quoted second-hand by Oregon Lookouts). Record height_m 24.4 is 80 ft; a correction to 27.4 is proposed for review. Elevation 941.8 m in the record matches the register's 942 m. Access is tribal land: the story tells visitors to ask the reservation first.
